doc.title: Buddy Tate interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995

title: Seeking an individual tone
summary: Tate says players of his day wanted to be identifiable by sound, like Herschel Evans.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Let me ask you this. You mentioned this other player, you mentioned his tone, and you said you liked his tone. Would you consider that you also have a signature tone, where people can just hear your tone and know that’s you? © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -3-

I try, I’ve tried for that to happen, and that’s what I hope is coming across because we in those days we tried to be individual, to be say, oh, yeah, that’s Buddy Tate, that’s Herschel Evans. So that’s what we tried to do then. And you know we didn’t want to like if you got the same teacher, if everybody sounded the same, you didn’t know who’s who. So we didn’t want it that way, you know? So I’ve tried to do it the way so they could say I could be identified.
